 Follow “Zombies” stars Milo Manheim and Meg Donnelly dedicate Kids’ Choice Awards win to late costar Carla Jeffery
 Jeffery, who played cheerleader Bree in the first three films, died Sept. 1 at 33.
 Shania Russell Mon, November 16, 2026 at 1:37 AM UTC 3 min read Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. Milo Manheim and Meg Donnelly at the Nickelodeon Kids' Choice Awards on Nov. 14, 2026
Credit: Francis Specker/CBS via Getty Key Points
 Zombies stars Milo Manheim and Meg Donnelly paid tribute to the late Carla Jeffery at the Kids' Choice Awards.
 The actors stepped up onstage after Zombies 4: Dawn of the Vampires won the "Watch Party" category and dedicated the award to Jeffery.
 Jeffery, who played peppy cheerleader Bree, died on Sept. 1 at the age of 33.
 Carla Jeffery will always be part of the Zombies family.
 Franchise stars Milo Manheim and Meg Donnelly expressed their love for their late costar on Saturday evening, after Zombies 4: Dawn of the Vampires won the "Watch Party" category at the 2026 Kids' Choice Awards.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "This is crazy," Manheim, 25, told the audience while accepting the KCA blimp alongside Donnelly, 26. "I want to take it to the message of the movie, which we shall never forget, which is acceptance, embracing others, your differences are your superpower, be unique, be you. It's been a crazy journey."
 After Donnelly stepped in to thank fans for their support, Manheim added, "We love you so much. We want to dedicate this award to Carla Jeffery."
 "We love you, Carla!" Donnelly concluded.
 The cast of 'Zombies' featuring Carla Jeffery (second from right) 
 Credit: Ed Herrera/Disney Channel 
 Jeffery, who starred alongside the duo as peppy cheerleader Bree in the first three Zombies films, died on Sept. 1 at age 33. A cause of death has not yet been disclosed.
 Advertisement Advertisement Jeffery's death was announced on Sep. 2 by her longtime manager, Carla Alexander, who shared a statement to the actress' official Instagram page remembering her as a "beautiful, vibrant, and incredibly talented woman whose radiant smile could light up any room."
 One day later, her family shut down rumors that drugs were involved in Jeffery's death, telling TMZ in a statement that "she did not do drugs."
 Prior to her death, Jeffery spoke openly about having epilepsy. She was inspired to go public with her health issues after suffering a seizure on the set of the first Zombies movie.
 Carla Jeffery at the premiere of 'Zombies 4' on July 8, 2025 
 Credit: Maya Dehlin Spach/Getty 
 "I want everyone to know not to be scared of who you are," she said in a 2022 conversation with the Epilepsy Foundation. "I've had this for years, and it's not going anywhere. I just have to work around it. I'm going to keep doing what I love, and at the same time, use my story to help others. I want to be an inspiration. I want you to know that you can do what you want to do despite it all."
 Get your daily dose of entertainment news, celebrity updates, and what to watch with our EW Dispatch newsletter . 
 Several of Jeffery's Zombies costars paid tribute to the actress following the news of her death. Manheim dubbed her the "sweetest person I have ever met" and Chandler Kinney wrote that she was "the brightest shining light in any room she walked into."
 Advertisement Advertisement A Houston native, Jeffery began acting at 12 and made her onscreen debut in the 2006 movie Phat Girlz as a younger version of Mo'Nique' s character. Her additional TV credits include Curb Your Enthusiasm , Shake It Up , iCarly , Good Luck Charlie , Crazy Ex-Girlfriend , and Scream Queens .
 Jeffery's twin brother, Carlon, is also a Disney star best known for his role in the series, A.N.T. Farm. He paid tribute to his sister one day after her death, sharing a heartbreaking screenshot of their final text exchange on Instagram.
